heatwave = a period of unusually hot weather lasting several days
drought = a long period with far too little rain
precipitation = rain, snow, sleet or hail that falls from the sky
humidity = the amount of water vapour in the air
torrential rain = extremely heavy rain that falls very fast
downpour = a sudden, heavy fall of rain
unseasonable weather = weather that is unusual for that time of year
mild winter = a winter that is warmer than usual
temperate climate = a climate that is neither extremely hot nor extremely cold
arid climate = a climate with very little rainfall
microclimate = the distinctive climate of a small area
prevailing wind = the wind that most often blows in a particular region
atmospheric pressure = the weight of the air pressing down on the Earth
climate change = long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns, largely caused by human activity
global warming = the rise in the Earth's average temperature
greenhouse effect = the way certain gases trap heat in the atmosphere
greenhouse gas = a gas such as carbon dioxide that traps heat in the atmosphere
carbon dioxide = a greenhouse gas produced by burning fossil fuels and by breathing
carbon footprint = the amount of greenhouse gas produced by a person, product or activity
ecological footprint = the amount of land and resources needed to support a lifestyle
